entities.name: Pig liver hydrodynamic gene transfer
observations: In vivo pig-liver hydrodynamic gene transfer can be limited by low transgene mRNA translation, but delivery route, vector persistence, and protein secretion also affect efficacy.

entities.name: Low translation in pig liver
observations: In live pig liver 24 hours after hydrodynamic eGFP plasmid delivery, retrograde injection produced substantial transgene mRNA but lower-than-expected translation; the authors concluded low RNA translation limited efficacy.

entities.name: PMID:25092576
observations: Compared anterograde and retrograde hydrodynamic plasmid delivery in pig liver and measured DNA, mRNA, and protein at 24 hours.

entities.name: Pig liver protein output
observations: Sealed-liver hAAT hydrofection produced approximately 4×10^5 protein copies per cell in pig liver versus 10^6 in mouse liver; lower plasma levels may reflect impaired pig-specific protein secretion.

entities.name: PMID:27695064
observations: Compared closed-organ hydrodynamic hAAT DNA delivery procedures in pigs and assessed tissue and plasma protein output.

entities.name: Route and vector effects
observations: In small pigs, hydrodynamic intrabiliary delivery gave lower vector copy number and luciferase expression than intraportal delivery; a replication-capable non-integrating vector increased genomes and luciferase about tenfold.

entities.name: PMID:35211639
observations: Compared hydrodynamic retrograde intrabiliary and intraportal gene transfer and vector designs in pigs.

entities.name: PMID:30220303
observations: ERCP-guided biliary hydrodynamic delivery transferred plasmid DNA to hepatocytes in all 12 pigs and enabled stable integration and protein expression.

entities.name: PMID:38338774
observations: Ex vivo hydrofection of isolated porcine livers produced detectable RNA transcription and human IL-10 plasma concentrations above 20 pg/mL through 10 days; inflammation was observed but not established as the primary limitation.

entities.name: PMID:33909609
observations: Evaluated ERCP-based biliary hydrodynamic delivery parameters in pigs; flow and pressure were tolerated and influenced tissue deformation, supporting delivery mechanics as an efficacy determinant.
